title: Crestline Flight Credits and Travel Vouchers: Reinstatement-Fee Basis by Value Restored
content:
**Accounting rule.** The reinstatement-fee basis of a credit of Crestline Flight Credits and Travel Vouchers is set from the value restored by the reinstatement. That value is the amount of the credit's restore entries, which bring back the value written off at its expiry.

- Value restored **below 250 US dollars**: the basis is 30 percent of the value restored.
- Value restored **at least 250 but below 600 US dollars**: the basis is the lesser of the instrument's reinstatement fee and 35 percent of the value restored.
- Value restored **600 US dollars or more**: the basis is the instrument's reinstatement fee.

## Bands of value restored

| Value restored (USD) | Reinstatement-fee basis |
|---|---|
| below 250.00 | 30 percent of the value restored |
| 250.00 to below 600.00 | the lesser of the instrument's reinstatement fee and 35 percent of the value restored |
| 600.00 and above | the instrument's reinstatement fee |

## Both sides of each band (hypothetical instrument whose reinstatement fee is 150 US dollars)

| Value restored | Working | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| 240.00 | 30 percent of 240.00 | 72.00 |
| 250.00 | lesser of 150.00 and 35 percent of 250.00, which is 87.50 | 87.50 |
| 400.00 | lesser of 150.00 and 35 percent of 400.00, which is 140.00 | 140.00 |
| 500.00 | lesser of 150.00 and 35 percent of 500.00, which is 175.00 | 150.00 |
| 600.00 | the instrument's reinstatement fee | 150.00 |

The value restored is read from the credit's own restore entries. A credit with no restore entry has restored no value.
